table: On-device gate — naive-vs-adaptive ASR gap, cross-platform (Check #4, UNSW-NB15 d=42 W=10, real surrogate, n=200)
gate_rule: Adaptive attacker must show a real gap over naive on the attacker-coupled basis (|gap| > 0.02) and none on the fixed PCA-2 basis, on-device, before any Pi adaptive-robustness number enters the paper.
note: Coupled-basis gaps match within ~0.03 abs across all 9 configs. The two x86 fixed-basis entries that marginally exceeded the 0.02 threshold (0.1/50 +0.035, 0.2/100 +0.045) land at +0.00 and -0.015 on the Pi, confirming they are run-to-run noise on both platforms, not signal.
takeaway: Adaptive attacker gains a large ASR edge through the attacker-coupled basis only (mean gap ~0.39 both platforms); the fixed PCA-2 basis yields no adaptive advantage (mean gap ~0.01 both platforms). The dev-box gate result transfers cleanly to real A76 silicon.
